**One same health cost: source-derived enhanced-rate reading.** Establish each route separately before applying a percentage: ordinary2.7.1 covers eligible professional health fees, rare-disease2.7.2 needs documented inclusion of the condition in the statutory state register and diagnosis/treatment expense, and ALS2.7.3 needs an evidenced ALS diagnosis/treatment connection. A diagnosis does not by itself prove professional-fee status or registry inclusion. Apply the first two routes’ own strict income test and their own annual caps; the ALS paragraph has no such income ceiling. For a single identifiable expense independently satisfying more than one of these cases, this method treats the specific20%rare or50%ALS rate as the enhanced rate **instead of adding**10%/20%again to that same cost. Use the ALS case for an evidenced ALS cost, including where rare-disease status is separately established; otherwise use the qualifying rare-disease case or ordinary case. Do not recycle the same expense above the selected branch’s cap into another branch in this one-cost worksheet. This is a labelled interpretation of the original2026amendment’s express explanation that the health deduction is raised to20%for rare diseases and50%for ALS, read with current2.7’s nested cases/common paragraph4. It is not a universal rule against claiming different tax credits, an express enacted election/incompatibility clause or a2026agency calculation ([current2.7](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOCT-c-2008-90028#a2); [Ley5/2026 preamble and art2.Dos](https://www.boe.es/buscar/doc.php?id=BOE-A-2026-10431)).

**Binding-cap same-invoice ledger.** A full-year2026Cantabrian45-year-old individual taxpayer, with no disability-cap increase or competing family claimant, has general BL28,000, savings BL0 and personal/family minimum5,550: income-test amount `28,000+0−5,550=22,450`, strictly below22,946. On15July2026 the taxpayer pays one5,000neurologist professional invoice by bank transfer for their own documented ALS diagnosis/treatment; the condition’s state-register inclusion is separately evidenced. None is covered/reimbursable, an insurance premium, a cash payment or an excluded public-benefit-association payment. Thus all three route definitions independently hold. The capped branch amounts are ordinary `min(10%×5,000,500)=500`, rare `min(20%×5,000,1,000)=1,000` and ALS `min(50%×5,000,2,000)=2,000`. Under the labelled enhanced-rate reading use **2,000once** for this invoice. With no other credits, the regional general quota is `1,985+(28,000−21,000)×14.5%−5,550×8.5%=2,528.25`: use2,000and leave528.25. Adding all three capped amounts would give3,500nominal and consume2,528.25, a different result ([own regional scale](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOCT-c-2008-90028#a1); [LIRPF74/77](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2006-20764#a74)). For the same facts with income-test amount exactly22,946, ordinary/rare fail their strict income gate while ALS still gives2,000: do not import their ceiling into ALS. The figures are a hypothetical source-derived2026ledger, not a software result or a real patient’s records.

**Exact remaining interpretation boundary.** The operative replacement separately says the taxpayer may deduct10%,20%and50%, gives separate ceilings and refers to three cases/deductions; it does not expressly state same-cost exclusivity or cumulation. That wording supports a competing cumulative-grants reading. The selected enhanced-rate method relies on the same enactment’s specific explanatory increase-to wording; a definitive ruling or operative2026agency worksheet resolving that tension has not been established here. The2025AEATmanual explains only the unchanged ordinary10%method and its income/payment gates, so neither it nor2025public software proves the new2026overlap. Keep a route-by-route expense ledger and the exact source reasoning; the competing statutory reading/challenge, allocations involving distinct mixed annual expense pools and shared-claimant/quota ordering beyond this one-cost individual example remain precise ordinary limits. The existing rates, separate non-overlap claims and payment/exclusion rules above remain applicable ([original enactment](https://www.boe.es/buscar/doc.php?id=BOE-A-2026-10431); [dated ordinary explanation](https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/ayuda/manuales-videos-folletos/manuales-practicos/irpf-2025-deducciones-autonomicas/comunidad-autonoma-cantabria/gastos-enfermedad.html)).

normalized_ops.old: **Finite priority qualification.** If insufficient quota forces a choice between current works credit and earlier works-credit vintages with different expiry dates, the read statute and these published instructions do not specify which vintage must be consumed first. The current-year total usage can still be `min(R,total valid works credit)` where no other reserved interaction changes it, but do not certify a favourable vintage/expiry allocation without an operative primary rule. For example, older350 expiring2030 plus current450 expiring2031 with `R=500` leaves300 credit in aggregate; it is either current300 expiring2031 if older amounts go first, or older300 expiring2030 if current amounts go first. Do not silently choose one. Multiple property expense-vintage allocation when a binding6,000 common annual base prevents all otherwise eligible tranches also requires that precise allocation analysis. Cases where all eligible expense tranches fit the annual ceiling and all valid credit is absorbed are fully computable by the stages above.
normalized_ops.new:
**Binding vintage ledger, labelled own-statute interpretation.** Paragraphs 22.7 and 23.5 expressly make a still-valid earlier quota-limited credit deductible during its four following years, until exhausted. Exercise that earlier carry right first within the same deduction type, charge it against the actual remaining quota, and then use the newly generated credit. Its residual is then unabsorbed because quota is exhausted, rather than voluntarily omitted while quota is available. For the supplied ordinary case, use the earlier expiry first and retain each origin and expiry in the return working papers. This is a disclosed reasoned application of the concurrent rights in these own provisions, **not a legislated universal FIFO rule**, an express agency vintage-allocation ruling or a formal election/change-of-election procedure. The sources name no compulsory current-first rule. They also do not establish that every other allocation is impermissible; a claim that a different order is legally compulsory remains a precise interpretation question ([own 22.7/23.5](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2011-18161#a5); [AEAT works balances](https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/ayuda/manuales-videos-folletos/manuales-practicos/irpf-2025-deducciones-autonomicas/comunidad-autonoma-galicia/gastos-derivados-adecuacion-inmueble-vacio-vivienda.html), [fixed-credit balances](https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/ayuda/manuales-videos-folletos/manuales-practicos/irpf-2025-deducciones-autonomicas/comunidad-autonoma-galicia/arrendamiento-viviendas-vacias.html)).

**Active 2026 works-credit separator.** A sole owner first leases one qualifying home in 2025 after 9,000 eligible, personally paid, invoiced costs. All existing vacancy, completion, value, tenant and continuing-rental conditions hold. Initial rent is 800 per month, so the separate 500 credit is unavailable; this does not disqualify the works credit. The 2025 permitted 3,000 base creates 450 credit; only 100 quota is available, leaving 350 of 2025 credit, last use 2029, plus 6,000 expense base. In 2026 another 3,000 of that original expense base creates 450 new credit. After other applicable deductions, available quota is 500. Apply the valid 2025 credit 350 first, then 150 of 2026 credit: carry **300 of 2026 credit, last use 2030**, plus the separately remaining 3,000 original expense base, last use 2027 under the single-home two-following-year rule. The 2026 aggregate usage 500 is the same under a current-first allocation, but that alternative would leave 300 of older 2025 credit expiring 2029. The supplied method identifies its actual selection and cannot report both favourable balances. For the earlier generic example with older 350 expiring 2030 and current 450 expiring 2031, the same disclosed selection leaves current 300 expiring 2031; the alternative current-first allocation leaves older 300 expiring 2030.

**Active 2026 fixed-credit separator.** A sole owner first lets home A in 2025 and home B in 2026, each previously empty for a year, on independent qualifying housing leases at 600 per month including annexes, to unrelated tenants. Both continuing-rental conditions and the maximum-three-home condition hold, and no works costs create a competing works credit. The 2025 fixed 500 credit used 200 of quota, leaving 300 with 2029 expiry. Available 2026 quota is 600: exercise that old 300 first, then 300 of home B's new 500; carry **200 of 2026 fixed credit, last use 2030**. Do not generate another 500 for home A merely because its lease continues. These are distinct claimant/home/credit-origin entries, not the works expense-base register.

**Binding multi-home expense-base selection, same labelled interpretation.** Paragraph 22.5 keeps amounts excluded by the combined 6,000 base available within four following years. Use the supported earlier-expiring eligible expense tranches first, within each home’s 3,000 annual and 9,000 total ceilings and the 6,000 combined annual ceiling, then admit current tranches to remaining capacity. The retained current expense is carried because the statutory base ceiling excludes it. The source grants those dated rights without specifying a compulsory within-base vintage priority. This method does not reclassify an already generated tax credit as expense, extend an existing expiry merely because the claim is carried again, or treat an omitted/unsupported invoice as automatically authorised carry ([own 22.2/3/5](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2011-18161#a5); [AEAT property/base capture](https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/ayuda/manuales-videos-folletos/manuales-ayuda-presentacion/irpf-2025/10-cumplimentacion-irpf-deducciones-autonomicas/10_11-galicia/10_11_20-gastos-derivados-adecuacion-inmueble-vivienda.html)).

A sole claimant has only three rentable homes A/B/C, each wholly owned, and no public aid. All qualifying works, vacancy, value, tenancy and continuing-rental facts are documented. A and B each incur 9,000 eligible costs, complete works and first let in 2025. C incurs 3,000 eligible costs, completes works and first lets in 2026. All rents initially exceed 700, isolating works relief from fixed 500 relief. There is enough regional quota to absorb every nominal works credit in this expense-base example. The 2025 two-home calculation admitted 3,000 for A and 3,000 for B; their remaining 6,000 each are genuine expense balances excluded by the combined ceiling, with 2029 expiry under 22.5. In 2026 each old home has a 3,000 annual tranche and current C has 3,000, so 9,000 competes for 6,000 capacity:

|2026 property tranche|Origin/last expense-use year|Eligible before combined ceiling|Base selected|Expense excluded by combined ceiling|
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
|A, earlier balance|2025/2029|3,000|3,000|0 of this annual tranche|
|B, earlier balance|2025/2029|3,000|3,000|0 of this annual tranche|
|C, current cost|2026/2030|3,000|0|3,000|

The selected 2026 base 6,000 generates **900** credit, fully used. After that use, A and B each retain 3,000 expense with the original 2029 expiry; C retains 3,000 expense expiring 2030. A current-first allocation would instead select C 3,000 and only 3,000 of A/B, leaving 9,000 of older expense expiring 2029. It would produce the same 900 current credit but a different expense ledger. In the supplied chronological selection, using A/B's last 3,000 each in 2027 and C’s 3,000 in 2028 gives 900 and 450 nominal credits, respectively; the total base across all years is 21,000 and total relief 3,150. None of the individual 9,000 lifetime property ceilings is exceeded. If the allowed 2028 C-base credit cannot be absorbed for quota, it is a **2028 credit** with 2032 last use; the original expense amount does not remain deductible a second time.

The ledgers need actual invoices/payment and grant records, property and claimant identity, qualifying first-lease year, original statutory exclusion, prior return/working-paper balances, amounts already used and continuing conditions. Neither an unclaimed grant nor a voluntary omission proves a carry trigger. Establish entitlement and any required original-claim correction instead of inventing a balance. The two rental credits began in 2025 under [Ley 5/2024 art. 2/DF3](https://www.boe.es/buscar/doc.php?id=BOE-A-2025-2145); [Ley 5/2025 art. 2/DF3.2a](https://www.boe.es/buscar/doc.php?id=BOE-A-2026-3385) makes the current works lease-year wording effective from 1 January 2025. The supplied hypothetical 2026 carry examples therefore use 2025/2026 origins, not fictional 2024 credits. Their last-use years do not restart on each annual use. The existing AEAT smaller-first rule **between the two deduction types** remains separate; the within-type fixtures above isolate one type. Mixed-type balances where a disputed reading of the amount used for that comparison changes priority, or equal-expiry property entries with different continuing-entitlement facts, require that precise additional attribution assessment. These are source-derived hypothetical calculations with stated upstream quotas, not official worked examples or real taxpayer records. No observed 2026 software result is asserted.

**Rural rental rehabilitation: grant ledger and completion-year day worksheet.** Establish the same claimant/property's eligible rehabilitation/finance costs and recognised public aid from invoices, financing/payment records and the award/certified-year schedule. Following [AEAT's exact base instructions](https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/ayuda/manuales-videos-folletos/manuales-practicos/irpf-2025-deducciones-autonomicas/comunidad-autonoma-extremadura/inversiones-rehabilitacion-viviendas-zonas-rurales-alquiler.html), first subtract the full recognised grant from total qualifying project investment, then apply the180,000total ceiling; do not subtract the grant again from an already net total. Separately subtract the grant share attributable to the current rehabilitation year from that year's eligible payments, then apply the9,040annual base cap per return and the remaining project-total ceiling. A single grant payment must be allocated across the actual rehabilitation years; the cash receipt date does not put the whole grant against that year's costs. The published instruction does not specify universal equal-year or cost weights. Use the supported award/certified-year allocation and reconcile its shares to the single grant; do not invent a favourable split where those documents do not establish one.

**Documented two-year grant example.** A sole claimant has14,000of independently eligible paid rehabilitation costs in2025and14,000in2026. A recognised12,000grant is paid once in2026; the award and certified-year schedule establish6,000attributable to each year's eligible costs. These year shares are stated documentary facts of this fixture, not a universal rule that every two-year grant is divided equally. Total net project investment is28,000−12,000=**16,000**, below180,000. Current2026net payments are14,000−6,000=**8,000**, so the annual base is8,000, assuming the total ceiling is not previously consumed and no other property uses the return's annual cap. Without this annual grant subtraction,14,000would instead hit9,040. Do not deduct all12,000from2026payments, which would give2,000, or treat16,000as the current annual base. The2025year's net-cost allocation is not proof that its credit was claimable before completion or that an unused2025amount carries into2026.

**Actual day framework, explicitly bridged from2025implementation.** The [official completion instructions](https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/ayuda/manuales-videos-folletos/manuales-ayuda-presentacion/irpf-2025/10-cumplimentacion-irpf-deducciones-autonomicas/10_10-extremadura/10_10_15-inversiones-rehabilitacion-zonas-rurales.html) ask separately for finish date, actual rented days and offered-but-vacant days after completion. In the public [RentaWEBOPEN2025, version1.19](https://www2.agenciatributaria.gob.es/wlpl/PARE-RW25/OPEN/index.zul?EJER=2025&TACCESO=COLAB), a fictional individual with10,000eligible annual investment and works finished31March2025received **986.18** for200rented+75offered days: `15% × min(10,000,9,040) × 200/275`. All275days rented instead gave1,356. With8,000annual net investment and the same200/75days, it gave **872.73**. A1January2025finish with300rented+64offered gave1,117.58; entering300+65was rejected because the day total must equal the days **after** completion. These actual separators support annual cap before the fraction, advertised vacancy outside the numerator, and the after-completion denominator rather than365. This is an inference for2026from the observed2025implementation of the unchanged9ter/agency instructions, not an observed2026return campaign or an expressly printed algebra ruling.

Apply that bounded framework to the2026grant fixture with works completed **31March2026**. Assume1April–17Octoberinclusive are **200**actual habitual-home letting days, and18October–31Decemberinclusive are **75**non-owner-caused vacant days, all unoccupied, available and advertised on property portals/agencies on qualifying terms. The tenant's early departure must preserve the statutory habitual-home status under an evidenced qualifying necessary-move exception; the landlord must continue the required five-year letting/advertised-vacancy undertaking and recapture on breach. For this example, assume the municipality's latest actual INE mean household income at accrual is an independently established30,000, so the annual advertised-rent ceiling is9,000; a700monthly offer annualises to8,400and passes. These are hypothetical verified-input assumptions, not a claimed income statistic for a named municipality. Preserve the real31Decemberpopulation/census evidence, dated INE release and offer terms, lease/nonrelationship/habitual-use evidence, dated finish certificate, rent/keys/advertisement records, proof the gap is not owner-caused, declared property income, grant allocation and sufficient regional quota. The credit is `round_to_cents(15% × 8,000 × 200/275)` = **872.73**. Counting advertised vacancy as actual rent would give1,200; using365would give657.53. Advertising preserves the qualified-gap treatment; it does not turn a vacant day into an actual rented day in this observed method.

**Timing boundary retained.** The same2025simulator rejected a31December2024completion with an explicit requirement that works finish in2025. Current9ter/agency text also speaks of annual rehabilitation/finance payments and the following five-year maintenance period, without an express completion-year-only entitlement sentence in the provisions read. The supplied positive example finishes in the claim year and avoids that conflict. Treatment of payments or financing in a different year from completion, pre-completion claims, zero post-completion days, and unearmarked/unequal grant-year weights remain precisely unconfirmed; no automatic carry, denial or blanket zero is substituted. The existing municipality, rehabilitation definition, five-year conditions and ownership/cost-allocation rules remain applicable.

The rural **own-home** credit is distinct:
